```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5)
```

This document introduces the Chicago Energy Benchmarking dataset, cleans it, engineers the features used
in Parts 2 and 3, and explores how greenhouse gas (GHG) intensity varies across buildings and over time.
The same steps are implemented in Python in `python/01_data_preparation_eda.ipynb`.

# 1. The dataset

Chicago's Energy Benchmarking Ordinance requires buildings of 50,000 sq ft or more to report their annual
energy use. The **Chicago Energy Benchmarking** dataset (City of Chicago Data Portal) holds those reports
for 2014–2023: one row per building per year, with property type, floor area, year built, number of
buildings, community area and location; electricity, natural gas, district steam, district chilled water
and other fuel use; site and source energy use intensity (EUI); ENERGY STAR score; Chicago Energy Rating;
and total and per-sq-ft GHG emissions.

```{r load}
raw <- read.csv("../data/chicago_energy_benchmarking.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                check.names = FALSE)
dim(raw)
cat("Distinct buildings:", format(n_distinct(raw$ID), big.mark = ","), "\n")
table(raw$`Data Year`)
sort(table(raw$`Reporting Status`), decreasing = TRUE)
```

# 2. Data quality

```{r missing, fig.height = 6}
missing <- data.frame(column = names(raw),
                      pct_missing = round(colMeans(is.na(raw) | raw == "") * 100, 1)) %>%
  filter(pct_missing > 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_missing))

ggplot(missing, aes(x = reorder(column, pct_missing), y = pct_missing)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Percentage of Missing Values by Column", x = "Column", y = "Missing (%)")
missing
```

**Interpretation.** Fuel-specific columns are mostly empty because few buildings use district steam,
chilled water or other fuels; a missing fuel almost always means the building does not use it. GHG
intensity and site EUI are missing for about a fifth of rows, mainly reports marked "Not Submitted" or
"Exempt". (Empty text fields are counted as missing here, so a few text columns show slightly higher
percentages than in the Python version.)

# 3. Cleaning

```{r cleaning}
df <- raw %>%
  rename(year = `Data Year`, property_type = `Primary Property Type`,
         floor_area = `Gross Floor Area - Buildings (sq ft)`, year_built = `Year Built`,
         n_buildings = `# of Buildings`, energy_star = `ENERGY STAR Score`,
         elec_kbtu = `Electricity Use (kBtu)`, gas_kbtu = `Natural Gas Use (kBtu)`,
         steam_kbtu = `District Steam Use (kBtu)`, chilled_kbtu = `District Chilled Water Use (kBtu)`,
         other_kbtu = `All Other Fuel Use (kBtu)`, site_eui = `Site EUI (kBtu/sq ft)`,
         ghg_intensity = `GHG Intensity (kg CO2e/sq ft)`,
         ghg_total = `Total GHG Emissions (Metric Tons CO2e)`,
         community_area = `Community Area`, lat = Latitude, lon = Longitude)
steps <- data.frame(step = "Raw building-years", rows = nrow(df))

# (1) Keep reports that contain the outcome and the energy intensity
df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(ghg_intensity), !is.na(site_eui))
steps <- rbind(steps, data.frame(step = "Has GHG intensity and site EUI", rows = nrow(df)))

# (2) Remove physically implausible values (data-entry errors)
df <- df %>% filter(between(site_eui, 5, 1000), between(ghg_intensity, 0.5, 150))
steps <- rbind(steps, data.frame(step = "Plausible EUI and GHG intensity", rows = nrow(df)))

# (3) Building characteristics needed for the models
df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(floor_area), !is.na(year_built), !is.na(lat), !is.na(lon),
                    floor_area > 0, between(year_built, 1850, 2023))
steps <- rbind(steps, data.frame(step = "Has floor area, year built and location", rows = nrow(df)))

# (4) One report per building per year
df <- df %>% arrange(ID, year) %>% group_by(ID, year) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
steps <- rbind(steps, data.frame(step = "One row per building-year", rows = nrow(df)))
steps
```

# 4. Feature engineering

```{r features}
# (a) Property types grouped into 10 categories with similar energy use
group_map <- c(
  "Multifamily Housing" = "Multifamily", "Residential" = "Multifamily",
  "Residence Hall/Dormitory" = "Multifamily", "K-12 School" = "K-12 school",
  "Office" = "Office", "Financial Office" = "Office",
  "College/University" = "Higher education", "Adult Education" = "Higher education",
  "Hotel" = "Hotel",
  "Retail Store" = "Retail", "Strip Mall" = "Retail", "Enclosed Mall" = "Retail",
  "Other - Mall" = "Retail", "Wholesale Club/Supercenter" = "Retail",
  "Automobile Dealership" = "Retail", "Commercial" = "Retail",
  "Supermarket/Grocery Store" = "Grocery",
  "Hospital (General Medical & Surgical)" = "Healthcare", "Other - Specialty Hospital" = "Healthcare",
  "Medical Office" = "Healthcare",
  "Senior Care Community" = "Senior living", "Senior Living Community" = "Senior living",
  "Residential Care Facility" = "Senior living")
df$property_group <- unname(group_map[df$property_type])
df$property_group[is.na(df$property_group)] <- "Other"

# (b) Size, age and number of buildings
df$log_floor_area <- log10(df$floor_area)
df$building_age <- df$year - df$year_built
df$n_buildings <- pmax(ifelse(is.na(df$n_buildings), 1, df$n_buildings), 1)

# (c) Distance to downtown (the Loop) in km
df$dist_downtown_km <- sqrt(((df$lat - 41.8781) * 111)^2 +
                            ((df$lon + 87.6298) * 111 * cos(41.88 * pi / 180))^2)

# (d) Energy mix: shares of total site energy (a missing fuel means none was reported)
fuel <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x)
total <- fuel(df$elec_kbtu) + fuel(df$gas_kbtu) + fuel(df$steam_kbtu) + fuel(df$chilled_kbtu) +
  fuel(df$other_kbtu)
df$elec_share <- fuel(df$elec_kbtu) / total
df$gas_share <- fuel(df$gas_kbtu) / total
df$district_share <- (fuel(df$steam_kbtu) + fuel(df$chilled_kbtu)) / total
df$has_energy_mix <- total > 0

# (e) Log versions of the skewed intensities
df$log_ghg_intensity <- log(df$ghg_intensity)
df$log_site_eui <- log(df$site_eui)

# Latest report per building, used for modelling
latest <- df %>% arrange(year) %>% group_by(ID) %>% slice_tail(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
cat("Clean building-years:", nrow(df), "  Buildings (latest year):", nrow(latest), "\n")
sort(table(df$property_group), decreasing = TRUE)
```

**Interpretation.** Cleaning keeps **`r format(nrow(df), big.mark = ",")` building-years** and
**`r format(nrow(latest), big.mark = ",")` buildings** (latest year each), the same counts as the Python
version. `r round(mean(latest$year == 2023) * 100)`% of the latest reports are from 2023.

# 5. Exploratory analysis

## 5.1 GHG intensity by property type

```{r by-type}
ggplot(latest, aes(x = reorder(property_group, ghg_intensity, median), y = ghg_intensity)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", outlier.shape = NA) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 35)) +
  labs(title = "GHG Intensity by Property Group (latest year, outliers hidden)",
       x = "Property group", y = "GHG intensity (kg CO2e per sq ft)")

by_type <- latest %>% group_by(property_group) %>%
  summarise(buildings = n(), median_ghg = median(ghg_intensity), median_eui = median(site_eui),
            total_ghg_kt = sum(ghg_total) / 1000) %>%
  arrange(median_ghg)
by_type %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1)))
```

**Interpretation.** Grocery stores (median
`r round(by_type$median_ghg[by_type$property_group == "Grocery"], 1)` kg CO2e/sq ft) and healthcare
buildings (`r round(by_type$median_ghg[by_type$property_group == "Healthcare"], 1)`) emit three to four
times as much per sq ft as multifamily housing
(`r round(by_type$median_ghg[by_type$property_group == "Multifamily"], 1)`), but multifamily buildings
produce the most emissions in total because there are so many of them.

## 5.2 Age, size and location

```{r age-size}
latest %>%
  summarise(age = cor(ghg_intensity, building_age, method = "spearman"),
            log_floor_area = cor(ghg_intensity, log_floor_area, method = "spearman"),
            dist_downtown = cor(ghg_intensity, dist_downtown_km, method = "spearman"),
            n_buildings = cor(ghg_intensity, n_buildings, method = "spearman")) %>%
  round(3)

latest %>%
  mutate(age_band = cut(building_age, c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100, 200), right = FALSE,
                        labels = c("<25", "25-49", "50-74", "75-99", "100+"))) %>%
  group_by(age_band) %>% summarise(median_ghg = median(ghg_intensity)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(age_band, median_ghg)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Median GHG Intensity by Building Age", x = "Building age (years)",
       y = "Median GHG intensity (kg CO2e/sq ft)")
```

**Interpretation.** As in Python, age, size and distance to downtown have Spearman correlations close to
zero with GHG intensity; property type is the main divider.

## 5.3 Energy mix by property type

```{r mix}
mix <- latest %>% group_by(property_group) %>%
  summarise(Electricity = mean(elec_share), `Natural gas` = mean(gas_share),
            `District steam/chilled water` = mean(district_share)) %>%
  arrange(`Natural gas`)
mix %>%
  pivot_longer(-property_group, names_to = "source", values_to = "share") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(property_group, levels = mix$property_group), y = share, fill = source)) +
  geom_col() + coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Electricity" = "gold", "Natural gas" = "firebrick",
                               "District steam/chilled water" = "slateblue")) +
  labs(title = "Average Energy Mix by Property Group (latest year)", x = "Property group",
       y = "Share of site energy", fill = NULL)
mix %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

## 5.4 GHG intensity trend, 2018–2023

```{r trend}
trend <- df %>% filter(between(year, 2018, 2023))
panel_ids <- trend %>% group_by(ID) %>% summarise(n = n_distinct(year)) %>% filter(n == 6) %>% pull(ID)
trend_tab <- trend %>% group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(median_all = median(ghg_intensity), reports = n(),
            median_balanced_panel = median(ghg_intensity[ID %in% panel_ids]))

trend_tab %>%
  pivot_longer(c(median_all, median_balanced_panel), names_to = "series", values_to = "median") %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, median, colour = series)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_colour_discrete(labels = c("All reporting buildings",
                                   paste("Same", length(panel_ids), "buildings every year"))) +
  labs(title = "Median GHG Intensity of Chicago's Large Buildings, 2018-2023", x = "Data year",
       y = "Median GHG intensity (kg CO2e/sq ft)", colour = NULL)
trend_tab
change <- trend_tab$median_balanced_panel[trend_tab$year == 2023] /
  trend_tab$median_balanced_panel[trend_tab$year == 2018] - 1
```

**Interpretation.** For the `r length(panel_ids)` buildings that reported in every year from 2018 to
2023, median GHG intensity changed by `r round(change * 100, 1)`%, matching the Python result. Part of
this decline likely reflects a cleaner electricity grid and the 2020 pandemic, not only building
upgrades.

```{r save}
keep <- c("ID", "year", "property_type", "property_group", "floor_area", "log_floor_area",
          "year_built", "building_age", "n_buildings", "community_area", "lat", "lon",
          "dist_downtown_km", "site_eui", "log_site_eui", "ghg_intensity", "log_ghg_intensity",
          "ghg_total", "energy_star", "elec_share", "gas_share", "district_share", "has_energy_mix")
dir.create("../data/processed", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(df[keep], "../data/processed/building_years_clean_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(latest[keep], "../data/processed/buildings_latest_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Saved", nrow(df), "building-years and", nrow(latest), "buildings\n")
```

# 6. Summary

The cleaned data and every summary above match the Python version. The two project questions are:

1. **Which building characteristics best predict a building's GHG intensity?** (regression)
2. **What distinct energy-use profiles exist among Chicago's large buildings?** (k-means clustering)
